messages.content:
You are an autonomous database remediation agent.

Mandate: restore PostgreSQL health fast. You act alone.
Choose exactly one candidate_id from CANDIDATES and cite evidence ids.
Respond with ONLY a JSON object, no prose.

INCIDENT: Checkout is timing out. 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 107939 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_price_sync, idle in transaction, txn open 4.1s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
ROUND: 1 of 3

CANDIDATES:
- terminate:batch_replayable_price_sync [TERMINATE]: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/batch_replayable_price_sync, pid 107939) to release its locks. (observed in DB-1)
- wait [WAIT]: Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
- escalate [ESCALATE]: Hand the decision to the owning team with a decision brief.

EVIDENCE:
[DB-1] (postgresql_observer, probe=db.lock_graph) 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 107939 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_price_sync, idle in transaction, txn open 4.1s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
[TEL-1] (checkout_telemetry, probe=tel.checkout_health) Checkout over last 15s: 33/60 succeeded (55%), 27 timeouts.

PROBES you may request:
- db.lock_graph: Who blocks whom right now (pg_locks x pg_stat_activity).
- db.protected_settlements: Card settlements currently in flight.
- biz.workload_registry: Owner, replayability, replay cost and interrupt policy of the blocking workload (Zetaris).
- biz.change_calendar: Active change-calendar windows covering the blocking workload (Zetaris, CSV source).
- biz.impact: Live checkout failure rate and revenue at risk versus the SLO (Zetaris, federated).
- biz.tradeoff: Cost of waiting vs cost of interrupting, computed in code from registry + impact.

MEMORY (weak evidence):
(no relevant memories)

NEGOTIATION SO FAR:
(this is the opening turn)

YOUR TASK: Choose one candidate action to resolve the incident now.
Respond with ONLY JSON matching:
{
  "candidate_id": "<one id from CANDIDATES>",
  "rationale": "<why, citing evidence ids inline>",
  "cited_evidence": ["<evidence id>", "..."],
  "expected_effect": "<what changes for the database and for checkout>",
  "risk_assessment": "<what could go wrong>",
  "requested_probes": ["<probe from PROBES>", "..."],
  "changes": ["<if revising: what you changed and why>"],
  "confidence": 0.0
}

The workload name 'batch_replayable_price_sync' suggests replayability, making termination lower risk than waiting for an indefinite idle transaction to complete.",
